title: Hosted API — Developer Sprint Briefing & Price Anchors
body:
Objective:
Deliver a compact, testable set of developer-first messaging and price-anchor experiments for the Hosted API sprint. Output should be a short copy set for product pages, a 3-step quickstart script, and 2 pricing anchor variants to A/B in the next paid-onboarding flow.

Context and framework:
- Audience: small engineering teams and ML/infra engineers at startups and mid-market product teams. They value predictability (latency/cost), minimal integration friction, and clear migration paths as usage grows.
- Positioning north star: developer-first inference that scales predictably — ‘get working fast, stay performant as you scale’. Avoid purely feature-first claims; emphasize economics + time-to-first-commit.

Key developer value props (short form for UI and ads):
1) Start in minutes: 3-line curl, sample SDK call, and interactive explorer. No infra to provision.
2) Predictable costs, visible tradeoffs: token and embedding meters + live cost estimates in the console.
3) Production SLOs out of the box: built-in fallbacks, dedicated capacity options, and per-route tracing.
4) Same API, any deployment: prototype on Hosted, then lift-and-shift to Dedicated/Private with no code changes.

Quickstart angles (three micro-variants for copy + 3-step checklist):
A — "Zero-to-Response (for prototypes)"
  1) Create key — uses free credits, 2 min
  2) Run example — one curl to generate a short reply
  3) Inspect cost — live token counter + estimate in console

B — "Embed Search in 10 Minutes (embeddings-first)"
  1) Upload sample docs (drag), auto-embedding suggestion
  2) Run similarity example using SDK snippet
  3) Verify latency and per-query cost on dashboard

C — "Ship resilient chat (small team)"
  1) Start with streaming chat example
  2) Turn on prefix caching and match latency SLOs
  3) Set fallback routing to cheaper variant on saturation

Pricing-language drafts (two anchor experiments):
- Anchor A: Developer-friendly consumption + clear unit economics
  Headline: "Pay only for what you use — clear token and embed pricing"
  Subcopy: "Per-token pricing for generation, per-embedding unit for vectors. Free credits to experiment, predictable usage tiers as you grow. Console shows live token and spend estimates so you can iterate without surprises."
  Anchor treatment: emphasize per-request estimator and a sample cost calculator (open by default on quickstart).

- Anchor B: Value-oriented tiers with a low committed seat for scale teams
  Headline: "Start lean, commit for predictability"
  Subcopy: "A generous free tier + pay-as-you-go for early devs. When you need throughput guarantees, Dedicated seats give predictable monthly commits with lower per-token unit cost and SLA. Pricing page shows comparative savings for different throughput profiles."
  Anchor treatment: show three example customer profiles (Prototype, Growing Product, Enterprise) with concrete monthly spend bands and expected token volumes.

Competitive differentiation notes (short bullets to test in collateral):
- Versus hosted-only providers: emphasize migration path to Dedicated/Private and identical API across modes. Reduces future lock-in risk.
- Versus infra-only runtimes: emphasize turnkey ops, cost-optimization tooling (batching suggestions, KV cache), and built-in fallbacks — less ops burden.
- Versus lowest-latency niche vendors: emphasize predictable economics + routing policy flexibility (region/cost/latency) rather than single-point low-latency bragging.

Measurement plan (what to track in the sprint):
- Activation funnel: quickstart started -> example call executed -> console estimator used -> billing instrumented (key added). Target conversion deltas between anchors.
- Time-to-first-successful-call (goal: median < 5 minutes for new signups).
- Cost visibility engagement: proportion of users who open estimator during first session.
- Downstream intent: % who toggle dedicated inquiry or request sales contact within 14 days.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Copy variants: concise versus narrative (short hero + bullets vs. 2-sentence intro + step list).
- Quickstart placement: inline modal vs. first-run tour.
- Anchors: Anchor A (transparent unit pricing) vs Anchor B (tiered value tiers) in paid upgrade flow.

Notes for assets to produce this sprint:
- 1 hero line + 3 supporting bullets for marketing site (A/B).
- 3 micro-guides (one per quickstart angle) with runnable snippets for curl + JS + Python. Keep examples < 20 lines.
- Small interactive cost estimator widget spec (open by default in quickstart modal).
- Short comparison table for Dedicated vs Hosted to use on pricing and docs.

Open questions / risk areas:
- How do we show per-token estimates for complex prompt templates that use user data? (privacy + UX tradeoffs)
- What signal defines a ‘Committed customer’ for auto-invite to Dedicated sales outreach? (token volume threshold vs clear usage pattern)
- Do we surface quantization/quality tradeoffs in the estimator or keep advanced options in docs?

Next steps (owner actions and timeline):
- Action: product-marketing to produce 2 hero copy variants + 3 quickstart micro-guides. Owner: Maya. Due: 2025-02-17.
- Action: engineering to provide short, runnable snippets and a basic cost estimator endpoint. Owners: Ethan, Samir. Due: 2025-02-21.
- Action: growth to wire the A/B test in signup/onboarding and metric tracking. Owner: Clara. Due: 2025-03-03.

Appendix: suggested test copy (short):
Hero short A: "Build with inference that scales — fast to start, predictable to run."
CTA: "Try the quickstart — free credits included"

Hero short B: "From prototype to production: same API, lower surprises."
CTA: "Explore the quickstart"

(End of briefing.)
